title: Isolate Q4 2025
prompt: Using `orders` (with `order_date` already parsed): set `q4` to the orders placed from 1 October to 31 December 2025 that were not cancelled. Set `coupon_share` to the share of `q4` orders that used a coupon, rounded to 3 decimals. Set `marketplace_coupons` to the number of orders in the whole table that came through the `"marketplace"` channel and used a coupon. Set `latest_ids` to a list of the `order_id`s of the 3 most recent orders in `q4`, newest first.
hints: Compare `order_date` with `"2025-10-01"` and `"2026-01-01"`, and combine masks with `&`, each in parentheses.
A coupon was used when `coupon_code` is not missing: `.notna()`. The mean of a boolean Series is a share; `.sum()` is a count.
`q4.nlargest(3, "order_date")["order_id"].tolist()` gives the newest three ids as a list.
explanation: Q4 2025 has 677 orders, of which 642 were not cancelled. Using "before 1 January" as the upper bound keeps every order on 31 December, whatever its time. 23.1% of those orders used a coupon, above the 18.8% average across both years, an early hint that promotions matter to the Q4 story. Counting with `(mask_a & mask_b).sum()` answers the marketplace question without building a filtered table. For the latest ids, `nlargest` on the date column (or `sort_values("order_date", ascending=False).head(3)`) both work.

checks.q4-clean: `q4` has no cancelled orders and nothing before October 2025
